CausalChain: Chronic liver injury → activation of CAFs → secretion of IL-6 (and HGF) → enhancement of stem-like properties in HCC cells → upregulation of metabolic enzymes → increased production of immunosuppressive metabolites (kynurenine, SAM, MTA) → induction of inhibitory receptors (PD-1, CTLA-4) and T cell exhaustion → immune evasion and therapy resistance
Hypothesis: In HCC, a combinatorial therapeutic strategy targeting both CAF-derived IL-6 signaling and the tumor cell metabolic pathways responsible for producing T cell‐exhausting metabolites (e.g., kynurenine, SAM, MTA) will synergistically reverse immune suppression, enhance T cell cytotoxicity and overcome resistance to current immunotherapies.
Abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is characterized by a highly complex tumor microenvironment (TME) in which chronic inflammation, fibrogenesis and intricate crosstalk among cancer cells, cancer‐associated fibroblasts (CAFs), immune cells, and endothelial cells promote tumor initiation, progression, and resistance to treatment. Emerging evidence indicates that CAFs release cytokines such as IL‐6 and growth factors like HGF to promote stemness and facilitate tumor cell reprogramming. In parallel, metabolic reprogramming of cancer cells leads to accumulation of immunosuppressive metabolites such as kynurenine, S-adenosylmethionine (SAM), and methylthioadenosine (MTA), which contribute to T cell exhaustion through the upregulation of inhibitory receptors (e.g., PD‐1 and CTLA‐4). Here we propose a novel hypothesis that simultaneous inhibition of CAF-derived IL-6 and tumor cell metabolic pathways responsible for the synthesis of immunosuppressive metabolites may synergistically reverse T cell exhaustion and restore T cell cytotoxicity, thereby overcoming immunotherapy resistance in HCC.
